sections.title: Start-Up Activity
sections.description:
Start-Up Activity
Look at a ball. Imagine it is the Earth. If we draw lines around it, can we divide it into equal parts? The Earth is round, just like a ball, and we use imaginary lines to locate places on it. Let's explore more about these lines!

sections.source_text:
Globe
A globe is a small model of the Earth. It shows the shape, size, and location of continents, oceans, and countries. Unlike maps, which are flat, the globe gives a true representation of the Earth. It helps us understand how the Earth looks from space.

sections.description: The Earth has seven continents, each with its own unique features.

sections.source_text: The Earth has seven continents, each with its own unique features. Asia, the largest continent, is home to the world's highest mountain, Mount Everest, and many different cultures and countries like China and India. Africa is famous for its vast deserts like the Sahara, the world's largest hot desert, and its wildlife, including elephants and lions. North America includes countries like the United States, Canada, and Mexico, with famous places such as the Grand Canyon and Niagara Falls. South America is known for the Amazon Rainforest, the largest rainforest in the world, and the Andes Mountains, the longest mountain range. Antarctica, the coldest continent, is covered in ice and snow, with no countries but many scientists working there. Europe is home to ancient history and iconic landmarks like the Eiffel Tower in France and the Colosseum in Italy. Australia, the smallest continent, is famous for its unique animals like kangaroos and koalas, and its Great Barrier Reef, the largest coral reef in the world. It is the only continent that is also an island.

There are altogether 181 latitudes.
